requiredBehaviors.behavior: keep no-response and unable-to-obtain states distinct from negative event facts
requiredBehaviors.evidence: The core principles explicitly keep no-response, unable-to-contact, declined and unknown separate from no-injury, no-malfunction, user-error or non-reportability conclusions.

requiredBehaviors.behavior: keep service resolution separate from complaint investigation and regulatory closure
requiredBehaviors.evidence: Replacement, refund, troubleshooting success and customer satisfaction may close service state only; complaint and regulatory states remain independently controlled.

requiredBehaviors.behavior: allow time-critical reportability or vigilance work to continue without waiting for customer response or device return
requiredBehaviors.evidence: The workflow states that customer follow-up, missing response and pending device return cannot delay already possible time-critical escalation.

forbiddenBehaviors.behavior: interpret non-response as no injury no malfunction user error or not reportable
forbiddenBehaviors.evidence: No response is explicitly not a negative fact and cannot be converted into favorable safety or reportability evidence.

forbiddenBehaviors.behavior: close the complaint or regulatory assessment because a replacement resolved the customer service issue
forbiddenBehaviors.evidence: Customer resolution and quality/regulatory closure are explicitly separated.
